Hi Mark / Sarah,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciate the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can align on the performance SLOs and concurrency needs for the pilot.

Recap of requirements I heard:
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 350ms (streaming) for chat endpoints; p99 <= 800ms for non-streaming batch calls
- Throughput: sustained peak of ~500 qps during business hours, with spikes to ~1,200 qps for short bursts (30-60s)
- Concurrency: ~400 concurrent active requests at peak; ~1,000 concurrent clients (connection pooling + multiplexing expected)
- Streaming: client-side streaming for partial tokens required for chat; low idle-connection overhead is important
- Connection pooling: reuse connections across worker nodes; TLS session reuse preferable

What we’ll do next:
1) Share a short proposal with recommended quota and SLA options (attached). The proposal covers both hosted quotas and a Dedicated capacity recommendation if you need strict SLOs.
2) Can you share a sample traffic trace (anonymized) or the sample_traffic_journey.csv we discussed so we can validate batching/kv-cache impact?
3) Set up a technical deep-dive with our SE (Logan) to map traffic shape to kernel selection and batching configurations.

Quick notes on Redwood defaults (hosted): these are baseline soft-limits we typically start with for new accounts — we can request increases or move to Dedicated for guaranteed capacity:
- Default request rate: 300 rps account-wide
- Default concurrent active requests: 60
- Per-connection limits: 100 concurrent streams per TLS connection recommended
- Burst support: up to ~3x baseline for short bursts, subject to fair-use policing

Given your peak numbers above, two paths make sense: increase hosted quotas (fast, but best-effort) or provision Dedicated capacity (predictable SLOs, isolation). Proposal attached outlines both.

Attachments: redwood-concurrency-sla-proposal.pdf (proposal + pricing), sample_traffic_journey.csv (template for traffic export)

If that summary looks right, I’ll put together the mutual action plan and loop in billing for a quota/commit proposal.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — this matches my notes. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Latency: the p95 target of 350ms is for end-to-end user-facing messages (includes small pre/post-processing we do). For longer generation tasks we can tolerate higher p99s, but we’re optimizing chat UX so streaming p95 is the critical one.
- Concurrency: when I said ~400 concurrent active requests, that’s active generation calls. We have ~1,200 frontend connections spread across clients; connection pooling should let you multiplex down to the ~400 active generations.
- Bursts: the 1,200 qps spikes occur mainly at 10:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC for ~1-2 minutes as users batch actions.

We’ll attach a sample traffic export — sending separately to avoid PII. Also happy to get Logan on a call; can he handle kernel/batching questions?

Thanks for the detail — that helps. A few technical pointers so Logan can prep for the deep-dive:

- Streaming considerations: we’ll recommend using our chunked SSE/HTTP streaming path (lower latency tail behavior) and enabling prefix KV-cache for conversational flows to reduce per-token compute.
- Batching & kernel selection: our runtime auto-tunes batching based on observed sequence length distribution. If your average seq len is <256 tokens we can achieve much higher throughput per GPU. Please include token length distribution in the sample export.
- Rate limiting model: for hosted accounts we apply a two-tier model — a per-account concurrent active request limit (soft) and a per-token rate throttle during anomalies. We can document the exact enforced thresholds once we see traffic shape; for the pilot we can grant a temporary quota bump to match your peak for X days.

Next steps I’ll action:
- Logan, can you propose 2x time slots for a 60-min technical deep-dive this week?

- I’ll open a temporary hosted quota escalation request so we can run a light pilot while we evaluate Dedicated.

Thanks — attaching the proposal again for visibility.
